Look back over everything named so far: carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins and
minerals. All five are food components that the body actively uses — for energy, for
growth, for repair, for defence, for the hundreds of processes that go on without our
noticing. Components that do this work are called nutrients.
The five major nutrients divide neatly by function:
• Energy-giving nutrients — carbohydrates and fats
• Body-building nutrients — proteins
• Protective nutrients — vitamins and minerals
Vitamins and minerals earn the name protective nutrients because they defend the body
against disease and keep it working properly. You need them in tiny quantities, and you
need them without fail.
This is why you are told to drink milk, eat green vegetables, eat fruit, and eat whole grains
rather than only polished ones — not because these foods are filling, but because they
carry the nutrients that nothing else will supply.
THINK-SPOT
Vitamin D is on the list, but one of its sources is not a food at all.
Which one — and what does that tell you about spending time outdoors?
